 Mann’s ‘Diwali gift’: 3% DA hike for Punjab employees, pensioners 
 Trending Karnataka Bus Fare Rise Delhi Murder Bombay High Court Pune techie suicide Patanjali Ghee Mahadev Betting App Karnataka Bus Fare Rise Delhi Murder Bombay High Court Pune techie suicide Patanjali Ghee Mahadev Betting App Karnataka Bus Fare Rise Delhi Murder Bombay High Court Pune techie suicide Patanjali Ghee Mahadev Betting App Mann’s ‘Diwali gift’: 3% DA hike for Punjab employees, pensioners 
 Vibhor Mohan / Nov 05, 2026, 00:07 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann Chandigarh: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann on Wednesday announced a 3% hike in dearness allowance (DA) for around 8 lakh state govt employees and pensioners, calling it a Diwali gift. The increase, effective Nov 1, will be reflected in Dec salaries and pensions. Mann said the decision has taken DA to 53%, up from 28% in 2022, when AAP govt assumed office. The cumulative 11-percentage-point increase announced over the past two months would benefit employees and pensioners by Rs 1,813 crore during the current financial year and provide an annual financial benefit of around Rs 3,988 crore, Mann said on X. “Employees are the backbone of our govt, and we are fully committed to their welfare, rights and overall well-being. Heartiest Diwali greetings to all employees and their families,” he wrote. Employee unions disagree. “It is not a Diwali gift. Govt has announced release of 3% of DA out of what is already due to us. We will hold a detailed press conference on the issue on Thursday,” said Sukhchain Singh Khaira, coordinator of Joint Action Committee of govt employees and pensioners. In Sept, state govt announced an 8-percentage-point DA hike, comprising two instalments of 4% each, taking DA from 42% to 50%. The decision followed weeks of employee protests and a meeting between Mann and representatives of employee organisations. “This is for the first time that any govt has increased DA by 11 percentage points within just two months,” Mann said. The move comes a day after Punjab and Haryana high court issued a contempt notice to chief secretary K A P Sinha over non-compliance with its Aug 3 directions. The court directed him to file a compliance affidavit within 10 days and appear in person at the next hearing on Nov 17. The CM said unlike previous govts, which frequently cited empty treasuries, his govt prioritised employee welfare and ensured that financial constraints never became an excuse for withholding their rightful benefits. Mann said when the AAP govt assumed office in 2022, a substantial financial liability relating to Sixth Punjab Pay Commission was already pending. “The benefits of the Sixth Punjab Pay Commission were supposed to be implemented from Jan 1, 2016, but its recommendations were implemented only in July 2021. Consequently, arrears amounting to around Rs 14,191 crore had accumulated for the period from Jan 1, 2016, to June 30, 2021,” he said. The state’s outstanding liability towards DA and dearness relief arrears payable to employees and pensioners has been pegged at Rs 22,818 crore for the period from July 1, 2021, to Sept 30, 2026, according to a status report filed by the chief secretary before the high court. Mann said that his govt had “systematically addressed” this long-pending financial liability and prepared a phased payment plan to clear the outstanding arrears of Rs 14,191 crore. “We gave priority to pensioners, and their arrears were released on April 1, 2025. The arrears of serving govt employees have started being released from April 1, 2026. So far, arrears amounting to Rs 4,891 crore have been released, and the remaining Rs 9,300 crore will also be paid,” he added. At a press meet later, Mann said he always preferred dialogue to address the pending demands of employees, and “our doors remain open for them at all times.” ‘Look at Capt’: Mann on 3 AAP turncoats Asked about the three AAP MLAs — Kunwar Vijay Partap Singh, Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Chetan Singh Jouramajra — who have joined BJP, CM Mann said politicians should remain loyal to their party, adding that politics was not merely about becoming an MLA. He said before joining the saffron party, the three should have taken note of former Punjab chief minister Capt Amarinder Singh’s remarks that BJP did not even consult him on political decisions concerning Patiala. Replying to a question about Congress MP Rahul Gandhi’s rally in the state, Mann said, “Everyone has the right to hold rallies.” ‘ED raids mean polls near' Reacting to the raids by Enforcement Directorate (ED) at the residences of Moga AAP MLA Amandeep Kaur Arora, CM Mann said ED raids mean that elections are around the corner. “They use these weapons close to the elections. Earlier, CBI had gone to Rajbir Singh (CM’s OSD) house. We believe that they won’t find anything. Let them conduct the raids. ED keeps coming.” Delhi smog: ‘Bid to defame Punjab’ On BJP accusing AAP govt of pollution in Delhi, CM Mann said paddy harvesting was still going on, especially in Malwa region, then how come smoke has already reached the national capital? “(BJP leader) Manjinder Singh Sirsa knows that Punjab has no role in Delhi pollution. It is merely an attempt to defame Punjab,” he said.
